messages.text: just survived my first week of the new semester 😮‍💨
congrats!! how's the new lab
chaotic but fun. my advisor already gave me three papers to read lol
three?? in week one??
welcome to grad school 🙃
ok you deserve a proper dinner this weekend then
haha maybe! depends on how fast I read
ok I finished paper #2 and I understood maybe half of it
half is a passing grade
LOL
what are you up to
pretending to work, actually watching cooking videos
send me the good ones
this guy makes noodles from scratch in 10 minutes
ok that's hypnotic
Finally turned in the lab report 😭
Congrats! How late did you stay up
Past 2am. I'm dead
Go to bed early tonight, no scrolling till 2am again
hahaha you got me, I'm literally scrolling right now
Next time you're on my campus, dinner's on me
deal, I'm holding you to that
Got called out by my advisor at group meeting today. kinda annoyed
ugh, what happened
my results didn't replicate and he made a whole thing of it in front of everyone
that's rough. doing it in front of everyone wasn't fair
want to vent on a call?
it's ok, typing helps. thanks for asking though
you're kind of good at this
free this saturday? there's a photo exhibit near your campus
Saturday afternoon works
perfect, 2pm at the main gate?
see you there 😊
Saturday was so fun, we should do that again
haha yeah
that dumpling place was the best part
busy week coming up, sorry if I'm slow to reply
no worries, good luck with it
Did you eat yet? That noodle place near you is open late
Not yet. Maybe later
Ok, no worries

score.reason: It's polite and low-pressure, but after their lukewarm 'Maybe later' it just backs off without warmth or a hook.

suggestions.text: Ok! Don't let the papers eat you alive, noodles first
suggestions.why: It echoes the running noodle joke from ‘this guy makes noodles from scratch’ and her ‘that's hypnotic’, so it feels playful and specific instead of a flat ‘no worries’.

reasons.emotion: After warning about a busy week, 'Not yet. Maybe later' reads as flat and noncommittal, not warm or upset.
reasons.intent: It's a plain answer to your dinner question with a vague maybe, no invitation or deeper motive.

overview.reading: You two are in a warm, flirty grad-school-crush rhythm: they keep coming back to you with lab stress and small wins, you offer care and a low-key invite, and the photo-exhibit meetup actually happened. After that, though, their replies get shorter and they pre-emptively flag a busy week, so the recent stretch reads more polite than eager.
